Form3 Partners With Coinbase Infrastructure to Bring Stablecoin Money Movement to Its Global Customer Base
summary:
Form3, a leading global fintech offering account-to-account payments technology, today announced it is using Coinbase infrastructure to bring stablecoin money movement to its global customer base, offering clients a single hub for money movement. 
Stablecoins are becoming increasingly popular thanks to their ability to enable off-hours cash movement, lower transaction fees, expanded local payments access and faster processing. However, financial institutions moving between fiat and these digital assets face the problem of having to stitch together multiple banking and crypto holding systems, resulting in additional integrations, fragmented processes and the need for manual intervention. This new initiative brings stablecoin payment capabilities into the existing Form3 platform that Tier 1 banks already rely upon.
Form3 customers with a regulated Coinbase account will be able to fund via fiat currency and then mint stablecoins in their Coinbase wallet through Form3’s API.
Form3’s payments platform serves as the financial fabric that enables customers to connect to payment rails across North America, the UK and Europe to deliver seamless instant payments. This new development extends this connectivity to support clients’ adoption of new forms of money, including stablecoins. Form3’s customers include leading Tier 1 banks and fintechs, including J.P. Morgan Payments, Barclays, Santander, and Klarna.
Dave Scola, US CEO at Form3, commented: “Digital assets, like stablecoins, are continuing to gain traction as an effective cross-border payment method. However, unless banks and fintechs have practical ways to integrate stablecoins into their offering, their benefits will be confined to theory only. 
Rather than building a separate asset stack, our focus is on leveraging our existing institutional-grade fiat payments infrastructure which our customers already rely on and collaborating with Coinbase, a market leader in this space, to enable our customers to unlock the value of stablecoins as part of everyday payment operations.”

content: Form3 has partnered with Coinbase Infrastructure to integrate stablecoin money movement into its global payments platform. The collaboration allows Form3 customers with regulated Coinbase accounts to fund via fiat currency and mint stablecoins using Form3's API, bridging traditional banking and digital assets for Tier 1 banks and financial institutions.

BKN301 and Mambu Team Up to Accelerate the Adoption of Modern Banking Technologies
summary:
BKN301 and Mambu today announced a strategic partnership, joining forces to accelerate innovation and commercial expansion for financial institutions and fintechs by enabling the adoption of composable banking architectures.
The partnership combines Mambu’s Intelligent Core with BKN301’s sovereign AI and data infrastructure. Mambu’s Intelligent Core brings together Mambu’s core banking platform, Mambu Payments and Mambu Agentic, a native layer of AI connectivity, specialised agents and autonomous workflows connected directly to the core.
The BKN301 Orchestrator extends governed AI across the entire financial operation, unifying data from every system, including legacy and third-party platforms, and running AI on infrastructure the institution owns and controls, with no data leaving its perimeter. Together, they create a flexible, composable foundation that reduces complexity and integration risk, increasing agility and enabling faster adoption of modern banking technologies.
The collaboration is closely aligned with the vision outlined in Mambu’s Prediction Report 2026, which highlights a fundamental shift in the financial industry: banking is no longer defined by balance sheets and physical branches, but by the technology that connects products, services, and ecosystems. In this context, composable banking emerges as a strategic imperative for institutions seeking to remain competitive, scalable, and resilient.
Through this transformative partnership, institutions adopting Mambu gain a more effective way to access and implement Mambu’s Intelligent Core, thanks to the BKN301 Orchestrator acting as an enablement layer.
As an additional benefit, financial institutions increase the resilience of their banking infrastructure through BKN301’s Data Decoupling. By standardising and normalising data from all backend sources into a single, governed and continuously updated foundation, BKN301 improves data consistency, operational transparency, and provides a robust base for advanced analytics and AI-driven use cases.
By joining forces, BKN301 and Mambu redefine how financial institutions approach digital banking, shifting from rigid, monolithic infrastructures to flexible ecosystems that evolve together with market demands and customer expectations.
“This partnership with Mambu reflects our shared vision of a more agile and accessible financial ecosystem,” said Stiven Muccioli, Founder & CEO at BKN301. “By combining Mambu’s cloud-native core with BKN301’s orchestration and data decoupling capabilities, we enable financial institutions to modernise faster, reduce complexity, and build AI-native, future-ready architectures without disruption.”
“This partnership is about removing friction for our customers,” said Patrick Rood, Director of Partner Business at Mambu. “BKN301's orchestration and data decoupling capabilities make it easier for institutions to adopt Mambu's Intelligent Core and get more value from it, faster and without the integration overhead that typically slows modernisation down.”

Enfuce Appoints Vanessa Schotes as Chief Operating Officer, Unifying Focus on Operational Excellence as the Business Scales
summary:
Enfuce, Europe’s card issuing and processing powerhouse, today announces that Vanessa Schotes will take on the newly created role of Chief Operating Officer alongside her marketing remit. After four years as Chief Marketing Officer, Schotes will own the end-to-end customer journey and the quality of service Enfuce’s customers experience, from onboarding and everyday support through to the operational controls that keep its service reliable.
Quality has always been Enfuce’s edge, and as the company scales, the appointment gives it a dedicated leader with a seat at the management table. Schotes will lead Customer Onboarding, Operations and Marketing, working across the business to set clear service standards, keep operations resilient and drive continuous improvement at every point where customers experience Enfuce.
Schotes will also play a greater role in Enfuce’s growth in the DACH region, where it works with customers such as Porsche and Crédit Agricole Deutschland, and partners such as Giesecke+Devrient (G+D). Earlier this month, Crédit Agricole Deutschland selected Enfuce as card processor and BIN sponsor for its Visa debit card.
Enfuce has been female-founded and led since 2016, with women in senior roles across its management team.
“As Enfuce grows, we need to make sure the way we operate and serve our customers develops at the same pace as our technology and commercial capabilities. I want us to be more predictable, proactive and efficient, and make Happiness Built In something our customers experience every day.
Vanessa knows our business and our customers, and she brings the leadership, customer focus and drive for improvement that I believe we need for this next phase. I’m confident she will challenge how we work and help us build an operations organisation that can scale with our ambitions.”
Denise Johansson
CEO and Co-founder of Enfuce
“Every card programme we run is a promise our customers make to their own customers, and quality is how we help them keep it. As COO, my focus is on clear service standards and continuous improvement at every point where customers experience Enfuce. I look forward to evolving our operational excellence even further as we continue to scale.“ 
Vanessa Schotes
Chief Operating Officer and Chief Marketing Officer of Enfuce

She will also support the company's growth in the DACH region.

Pliant Secures More Than €200 Million in Additional Financing Capacity to Support European Growth
summary:
Pliant, a global fintech specializing in highly modular B2B payment solutions, today announced that it has secured more than €200 million in additional debt financing capacity through three transactions with Ascory Bank AG and Viola Credit. The financing strengthens Pliant's ability to support growing credit card payment volumes and customer credit card lines across Europe, providing a scalable refinancing foundation for its continued expansion.
The financing structures are designed to address the distinct liquidity requirements of commercial card issuing, including funding customer credit balances and meeting card scheme settlement collaterals. By securing secured financing against both, Pliant can support greater transaction volumes while maintaining a scalable and efficient funding model.
The transactions include two facilities provided by Ascory Bank, a long-standing partner of Pliant. The first uses a securitization structure backed by receivables from Pliant's European corporate credit card business. The second supports collateral requirements associated with Visa's card settlement process (Visa Prefunding Solution), helping Pliant manage the liquidity needed to support increasing card transaction volumes.
The third transaction extends Pliant's existing growth debt facility with Viola Credit, including an option to increase financing capacity. Together, the arrangements provide additional financial flexibility and are expected to support Pliant's anticipated European growth over at least the next two years.
“As our European business continues to scale, it's critical that our financing infrastructure grows alongside it,” said Malte Rau, CEO and co-founder of Pliant. “These agreements give us significantly greater capacity to support our customers' payment needs while continuing to expand our commercial card business. They also reflect the strength of the financial infrastructure we've built and the confidence our financing partners have in Pliant's long-term growth.”
“We have worked with Pliant for more than six years, so it is particularly rewarding to see how our partnership has developed over time,” said Lukas Diehl, Head of Corporate Clients at Ascory Bank. “During that period, both Pliant and Ascory have grown significantly, while maintaining the trust and close collaboration that have characterized our relationship from the beginning. With this financing, we are taking the next step and providing Pliant with a flexible solution that supports its continued growth.”
“We’re excited to continue backing Pliant as the company expands into new markets while maintaining a strong European presence,” Elad Friedman, Managing Director at Viola Credit. “Over the past years Pliant has emerged as the leading Europe HQed provider of corporate credit card solutions, and together with the new capital raise will continue its growth into new verticals and markets.”
The announcement follows Pliant's recently announced $80 million Series C funding round, which will support further international expansion and development of its AI-powered payment infrastructure. The new debt financing arrangements complement that investment by providing additional capacity to support Pliant's growing European commercial card business.

Zopa Bank Joins Warm Homes Loan Scheme to Help Millions of Brits Cut the Cost of Green Home Upgrades
summary:
Zopa, the British digital bank pioneer with 2 million customers, has joined the government’s Warm Homes Loan Scheme to help eligible customers lower the cost of their green home upgrades. 
Zopa is offering eligible customers lower-cost financing on heat pumps, solar panels, and solar battery storage at rates ranging from 3.6% to 4.6% APR over 3 to 10 years, available through participating installation partners. 
For example, a customer borrowing £10,000 over 10 years at 4.6% APR would pay £25.61 less each month than on an equivalent loan at 9.9% APR, cutting total interest costs by 55.7% and saving the customer approximately £3,073 across the full term.*
Applications for Zopa finance are subject to eligibility, credit and affordability checks.
The announcement comes as more households and businesses invest in technology to generate and store energy than ever before. There were around 36,000 certified battery storage installations across the UK in the first half of 2026 alone, almost double the number recorded in the same period a year earlier.
Making these technologies more affordable will be key to sustaining that momentum. For many customers, however, the upfront cost remains a barrier to making these improvements. 
Tim Waterman, Chief Commercial Officer at Zopa Bank, said: “Everyone should have the opportunity to live in a home that’s warmer, greener and more affordable to run. But for too many households, the upfront cost of technologies like heat pumps and solar panels stands in the way of that transition.
“By joining the Warm Homes Loan Scheme, Zopa is helping to turn the ambition for a warmer, more affordable home into reality. By bringing down the cost of finance and giving eligible customers the option to spread payments over up to 120 monthly instalments, we’re enabling more people to take greater control of their energy use, offering more choice over how they pay alongside reassurance of a fully regulated experience.”
Minister for Local Jobs and Energy Minister McCluskey said: “Zopa Bank joining the Warm Homes Loan Scheme is great news for consumers, as we have seen significant demand since we launched last month.
“Low and no interest loans allow people to benefit from clean energy tech such as solar, heat pumps and batteries - with no upfront costs - so more families can save on their bills.”
The news further supports Zopa’s entry into green lending and Zopa for Business' provision of more payment and finance tools for UK businesses.
In 2024, Zopa partnered with Octopus Energy to enter the £23bn renewable energy market; in 2026, it has partnered with Hive Energy and Segen to give customers more financing options when upgrading their homes.
This year’s partnerships launched alongside Zopa for Business, Zopa’s bolstered business offering that brings payments, retail finance, auto finance and embedded partnerships into a single platform.
Designed to help businesses accept payments, offer finance and complete more sales by integrating once without juggling multiple providers, it follows Zopa’s acquisition of payments platform Rvvup in 2025 and point-of-sale finance platform DivideBuy in 2023.
These developments contribute to Zopa’s sustained profitable growth, having originated £1.6 billion in new lending in the first half of 2026, up 35% year on year. As a result, Zopa is now the UK’s largest open-market lender for personal loans by volume and among the top three by value. 
One of the UK’s highest rated and most celebrated financial brands, Zopa has been recognised with over 10 British Bank Awards, holds a Trustpilot rating of 4.6/5, and has one of the highest customer satisfaction scores in the industry.

The digital bank is offering reduced interest rates to help eligible customers cut upfront costs, lower energy bills, and make their homes more energy efficient. This move supports Zopa's broader expansion into renewable energy and green lending.

title: Cytora and GBG Partner to Bring Identity and Financial Crime Checks Into Commercial Underwriting
summary:
Cytora, the risk digitization and automation platform for commercial insurance, and GBG, the AI trust intelligence platform, today announced a partnership that puts identity verification, business verification and financial crime screening inside Cytora's risk workflows. 
Every commercial submission raises two questions before anything else can happen: who is this, and can we do business with them? Today those answers usually arrive late, assembled by hand from company registries, sanctions lists and internal checks, often after an underwriter has already formed a view. Under this partnership, they arrive with the submission.
As each risk is digitized, the Cytora platform queries GBG to resolve the insured entity and return:
Identity verification (KYC): confirms the individuals behind the business are real and correctly identified
Business verification (KYB): confirms the entity exists, and shows its structure and [ultimate ownership, where available by jurisdiction]
Sanctions, PEP and AML screening: checks against global watchlists, with the evidence attached to the record
The result is a decision-ready risk that can be evaluated against the insurer's own appetite rules. Clean risks flow through to straight-through processing. Anything that warrants a closer look is routed to specialist review with the supporting evidence already gathered, so the reviewer starts from a position of knowing rather than asking. Because the checks run inside the workflow, every one of them is logged and auditable.
For insurers writing financial lines, commercial package, specialty and other complex risks, this turns due diligence from a task performed after submission into a control that operates during it, without adding a step for the underwriter.
GBG joins Cytora's Data Partner Ecosystem as its identity and financial crime intelligence partner. 
The partnership adds a capability that has been largely absent from the commercial insurance data landscape. Cytora's ecosystem already spans property, climate, cyber, financial and geospatial data; identity and financial crime intelligence completes the picture at the point where every risk relationship begins.
Zurich scaled Cytora's agentic AI to five countries in 90 days and is scaling AI-powered risk digitization across 20+ markets within the first 16 months, reducing manual processing time by over 80 per cent. GBG supports more than 20,000 customers worldwide and processes around 800 million identity checks a year.
“Every risk decision starts with knowing who you are dealing with. With GBG in our Data Partner Ecosystem, insurers can verify the entity and screen for financial crime as the submission is digitized, so underwriters start from a verified risk, not a question.”
Juan De Castro, COO, Cytora
“Financial crime checks shouldn't be the step that slows an underwriter down, or the one that gets skipped when the queue is long. Inside Cytora, they run as each submission arrives. Clean risks move. The ones that deserve a closer look get one, with the evidence already attached.”
Gus Tomlinson, Chief Product & Technology Officer, GBG

content: Cytora, a risk digitization platform for commercial insurance, has partnered with AI trust intelligence platform GBG. The collaboration integrates identity verification, business verification, and financial crime screening directly into Cytora's risk workflows. By automating these essential checks upon submission, insurers can improve due diligence, accelerate decision-making, and enhance compliance without adding manual steps for underwriters.
